_readme: Copy this file to appsettings.json NEXT TO GtBridge.exe to configure a bridge
installation without rebuilding it. Every key is OPTIONAL: an omitted key falls
back to the environment variable, and then to the value compiled in as the
default, so a bridge with no appsettings.json at all behaves exactly as it did
before this file existed.
Precedence, highest first:  OL_BRIDGE_* environment variable  >  this file  >  built-in default.
The environment-variable name is the key upper-snake-cased and prefixed, e.g.
SqlServer -> OL_BRIDGE_SQL_SERVER, SferaOperator -> OL_BRIDGE_SFERA_OPERATOR.
SqlConnectionString overrides SqlServer/SqlDatabase entirely - use it when the
installation needs SQL authentication rather than the integrated security the
composed default assumes.
ApiUser/ApiPassword guard the WooCommerce-dialect shim routes; InvoiceToken
guards the /api/* routes (Bearer or x-bridge-token). These three have NO
built-in default: unset leaves the routes they guard CLOSED, because a
credential compiled into a binary is a credential everybody has.
The CHANGE-ME values below are recognised as placeholders and count as UNSET,
so copying this file and forgetting to edit it leaves those routes closed
rather than guarding them with a secret printed in a public repository. The
bridge warns at startup naming each key still left at its stand-in.
CertificatePath/CertificatePassword likewise have no default, and are left
EMPTY here on purpose: a stand-in path made HttpsConfigured true and the
process died binding a certificate that does not exist, which is neither of
the two documented behaviours. Unset means the HTTPS listener is not opened;
the plain-HTTP port still serves, and that is the port OpenLinker reaches the
bridge on. A path that IS set but wrong is refused at startup, by name.
